title: Choose the look for Bible Reading 2027
question: The roll picked the Date-Due Card. Keep it, take another, or re-roll.

options.label: Date-Due Card
options.lineage: library date-due slips and rubber date stamps
options.thesis: Each reading you finish is stamped with the day you read it.
options.viewport: Today's three readings as rows on a date-due card; checking one stamps today's date in your ink, your partner's stamp sits beside it in theirs.
options.risk: Turns into a library costume if the card frame or stamp texture gets decorative.

raised.raise: References are set big enough to be the interface, with no card chrome around them.
Stamp ink is reserved for finished readings; nothing else on screen uses it.
Each track keeps one fixed identity across Today, Week and Plan.
Every day carries its place in the sequence: day 1 of 260.
Today is one complete day; the next day is one swipe away.
Hierarchy comes from type scale, not boxes or fills.

options.label: The Plan Sheet
options.lineage: printed reading-plan checklists tucked inside a Bible
options.thesis: The paper checklist you keep in your Bible, made live and shared.
options.viewport: Today's readings on top with large tick boxes, and the whole week's grid of 15 boxes underneath for both of you.
options.risk: The most familiar option here; it can slide into a plain to-do list.

options.label: Metro Tiles
options.thesis: Giant cropped type and flat color tiles as the whole interface.
options.viewport: Readings as color tiles on black.
options.risk: Reads as a phone OS, not a Bible companion.
options.case: Fuses poorly: readers don't recognize themselves in it and tiles hide the references.

options.label: Orienteering Map
options.thesis: The year as a course with one purple leg for today.
options.viewport: Weeks as controls on a course.
options.risk: A sport metaphor most readers won't know.
options.case: Fuses poorly: unfamiliar to the audience and adds a map to a simple list.
options.kept: One ink reserved for the active leg.

options.label: Transit Diagram
options.thesis: Three tracks as three colored lines with a station for each day.
options.viewport: NT, OT and wisdom as lines meeting at today.
options.risk: Turns a three-item list into a diagram to decode.
options.case: Clear for the year view but slower than a list for today, and not the readers' world.
options.kept: Each line keeps one fixed identity everywhere.

options.label: Catalog Sleeve
options.thesis: Every day a catalog number on matte black.
options.viewport: A coded strip for each day.
options.case: Fuses poorly: coded labels fight a glance-and-go task.

options.label: Vertical Feed
options.thesis: One day fills the screen; swipe for the next.
options.viewport: Today full screen with a rail of actions.
options.risk: Borrows the feel of an attention app the product opposes.
options.case: Fuses poorly: invites scrolling when the goal is closing the app and opening a Bible.

options.label: Type Specimen
options.viewport: One reference huge, the rest small.
options.risk: A type demo, not a tool.
options.case: Fuses poorly: nothing in it is about reading together.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean phone checklist app, done well.
canonCard.viewport: A grouped list of today's readings with system checkmarks.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from any to-do app by design.
